title: Mining, luck, and building a settlement: my first playable prototype, made while learning to code with AI
author: Extension-Mammoth252
selftext:
I work 12-hour rotating shifts, and when I'm off, my favorite thing lately has been coding with AI. I'm still learning all of it, and honestly it's been amazing.

I've always loved mining games. You chip away, you get your rewards, and every once in a while something lucky surprises you. I also love build progression and atmosphere. So I'm making a game that blends all of that: mine, chop, explore, and build up a small frontier settlement.

[Our first camp](https://preview.redd.it/0lim6wpkqcsh1.jpg?width=2275&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=18af850ec1f5cff27299b2f0715c6b647a68f6e8)

The 'lucky' part: every so often, ordinary mining turns up a surprise: a rock or ore vein cracks open to reveal a huge pocket of materials, with its own little moment when it happens. Buildings go up in stages as you bring materials, and crafting stations like the Smithy come to life as you build them.

**How I'm making it**

I'm using several AIs together, some for planning and prompting, some for coding, some for both:

* Claude Code does the building and coding in Godot 4.7
* A separate Claude chat acts as a creative director: reviewing the work, pushing back, and helping me write prompts
* GPT Image for concept art, Tripo to turn concepts into 3D models, cleaned up in Blender

**A few things I've learned so far**

* What looks right in a close-up screenshot doesn't always work at gameplay distance. My rocks only started reading well once we painted the lighting directly into the textures.
* AI will happily tell you something is done. Having a second AI review the work catches a lot.
* Godot packs every file in your project into the build by default. My first build was 1.9 GB of mostly unused files, and cleaning that up cut about 600 MB.

It's an early prototype, so expect rough edges. I'd love feedback, especially on how the mining feels and the overall look.
